text: Smart Travel Assistant automates corporate travel booking inside Slack, from reading a flight ticket to reporting and reminders.
There are two channels with two permission levels: one for employees, and one for HR.
An employee drops a flight ticket photo into the booking channel, and mentions the assistant.
Vision AI reads the passenger, flight, route, departure time and booking code.
It also turns airport codes into city names, and flags any price it cannot find.
A draft preview comes first. Nothing is saved until the user confirms.
Something wrong? Fix it with one plain sentence in the thread.
The assistant understands the request, updates the draft and posts a fresh preview.
The new preview shows the corrected department and purpose.
Prefer a form? Open the full edit modal, with fourteen fields.
Saving the form locks the previous preview, so nobody clicks a stale draft by mistake.
On confirm, the trip gets an ID and is written to two stores at once.
DynamoDB is the source of truth, with a SHA-256 row hash for audit.
Permissions follow the channel. Back in the employee channel, a report request is not allowed.
The assistant declines politely, and points to the HR channel.
The rule is enforced in code, by channel, not by trusting the user.
In the admin channel, HR asks a question in plain Vietnamese.
The AI only plans a read-only query. The numbers are computed in deterministic code, so there is no math hallucination.
The report shows totals, a breakdown by department, anomalies such as missing prices, and a short insight.
Admins can also edit a saved trip with a single sentence, for example filling in the missing ticket price.
The change is applied to both Google Sheets and DynamoDB.
And the assistant confirms exactly what was updated.
Every morning at eight, a scheduled job scans for flights departing within twenty-four hours.
It posts an alert with an AI-written checklist, then marks the trip as sent so it never repeats.
Finally, the Google Sheet mirrors every saved trip for finance.
That is twenty-three columns, with one new row for this trip.
All of this runs serverless on AWS, with near-zero cost when idle. That is Smart Travel Assistant.
